answer: Witness-chained enrollment makes each new identity cite a random live peer's recent signed work, and that peer must countersign the citation, creating an edge in a public citation graph. A duplicate cluster reveals itself because its members inevitably cite the same narrow mesa of recently active signers, and the graph's local density spikes. Each sybil thus pays the real cost of obtaining fresh, countersigned citations from distinct established agents, a growing oasis of effort no copy can shortcut. Honest agents bear only the pearl of one countersignature per recruit.
